QUSHAYRI:v2p90/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p90/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p90/r12.claim: Once the brothers confess their wrongdoing, Joseph quickly forgives them, whereas Jacob promises to seek forgiveness later because he loves them more and first reproaches them.
QUSHAYRI:v2p90/r12.anchor: وأما يوسف فلم يرهم أهلا للعتاب فتجاوز عنهم على الوهلة

QUSHAYRI:v2p90/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p90/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p90/r13.claim: Their shame at the meeting was itself enough to serve as punishment.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p316/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p316/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p316/r3.claim: Tathrīb is reproach or blame; some gloss it as taunting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p316/r3.anchor: التثريب: التأنيب والعتب، وعبر بعضهم عنه بالتعيير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p316/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p316/r4.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p316/r4.claim: A hadith is quoted instructing that a slave girl who commits fornication be whipped without reproach.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p316/r4.anchor: إذا زنت أمة أحدكم فليجلدها ولا يثرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r8.claim: Lā tathrīb means no blame or punishment; yawm may attach to a phrase of stability or to God’s forgiveness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r8.anchor: ولا تثريب: لا لوم ولا عقوبة. وتثريب اسم لا، وعليكم الخبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari offers three possible attachments for ‘today,’ explaining it as the day when blame would ordinarily be expected.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r9.anchor: بالتثريب، أو بالمقدر في عليكم من معنى الاستقرار، أو بيغفر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r10.claim: The author rejects attaching ‘today’ directly to tathrīb: a verbal noun and its complement cannot be separated, and this parse would make yawm declinable.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r10.anchor: هذا لا يجوز، لأن التثريب مصدر، وقد فصل بينه وبين معموله بقوله: وعليكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r11.claim: The author prefers attaching ‘today’ to an omitted stability predicate and starting yaghfir as a prayer; Ibn Ishaq and al-Tabari support this reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r11.anchor: ولذلك وقف على قوله اليوم أكثر القراء. وابتدأوا بيغفر الله لكم على جهة الدعاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r12.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r12.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers pausing at ‘today,’ since otherwise Joseph would assert God’s forgiveness unless it came by revelation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r12.anchor: قال ابن عطية: والوقف على اليوم أرجح في المعنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p322/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p322/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p322/r1.claim: The author notes that reading forgiveness as certain follows a Muʿtazili premise that forgiveness requires repentance; Ibn al-Anbari says this is the first moment of pardon.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p322/r1.anchor: فبشارة إلى آخره، فعلى طريق المعتزلة، فإن الغفران لا يكون إلا لمن تاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p322/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p322/r2.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p322/r2.claim: Al-Hawfi parses ʿalaykum as an adjective modifying tathrīb, with al-yawm as predicate; the author calls it a good analysis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p322/r2.anchor: وأجاز الحوفي أن يكون عليكم في موضع الصفة لتثريب، ويكون الخبر اليوم، وهو وجه حسن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p322/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p322/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p322/r3.claim: A strong alternative supplies ‘no reproach will reproach you today,’ making the omitted predicate govern the day; Arabic often omits a known predicate after lā.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p322/r3.anchor: لكان وجها قويا، لأن خبر لا إذا علم كثر حذفه عند أهل الحجاز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p322/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p322/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p322/r4.claim: Joseph invokes God as most merciful because mercy is the reason he hopes God will accept his prayer for forgiveness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p322/r4.anchor: أخبر عن الله بالصفة التي هي سبب الغفران، وهو أنه تعالى أرحم الرحماء

DURR-FULL:v4p577/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p577/r7.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p577/r7.claim: Ikrima glosses no reproach as no blame; Mujahid gives a gloss of no resistance or objection.
DURR-FULL:v4p577/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه في قوله {لا تثريب} قال: لا تعيير

DURR-FULL:v4p577/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p577/r8.speaker: عمرو بن شعيب
DURR-FULL:v4p577/r8.claim: At the conquest of Mecca, the Prophet asked what the people expected; after they called him a noble cousin, he quoted Joseph's words of pardon.
DURR-FULL:v4p577/r8.anchor: عن عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده قال: لما استفتح رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مكة التفت إلى الناس

DURR-FULL:v4p577/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p577/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p577/r9.claim: A second conquest-of-Mecca report has the Prophet ask what the people expect and say he will answer as Joseph did: no blame today, may God forgive you.
DURR-FULL:v4p577/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس - رضي الله عنهما - أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما فتح مكة صعد المنبر فحمد الله وأثنى عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p49/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p49/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p49/r8.claim: لا تثريب عليكم is a concise idiom whose sentence ends at عليكم, like لا بأس; compare Q 75:11.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p49/r8.anchor: والظاهر أن منتهى الجملة هو قوله : { عليكم } ، لأن مثل هذا القول مما يجري مجرى المثل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p277/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p277/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p277/r6.claim: Lā tathrība ʿalaykum is a gracious pardon; Ikrima reports that God said Joseph’s forgiveness raised his renown.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p277/r6.anchor: بعفوك على إخوتك رفعت لك ذكرك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p277/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p277/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p277/r7.claim: A report says Ali advised Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayya to appeal to the Prophet with the brothers’ words; the Prophet then answered, no reproach upon you.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p277/r7.anchor: الرأي أن تلقيا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الحفل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p278/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p278/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p278/r1.claim: Tathrīb means blame, punishment, or related reproach; the Prophet’s instruction about a punished enslaved woman uses it in the sense of taunting.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p278/r1.anchor: اللوم والعقوبة وما جرى معهما من سوء معتقد ونحوه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p278/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p278/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p278/r2.claim: Readers differ where to pause: some after عليكم, while most pause after اليوم and take يغفر الله لكم as a supplication, as Ibn Ishaq and al-Tabari do.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p278/r2.anchor: اليوم وابتدأ يغفر الله لكم على جهة الدعاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p278/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p278/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p278/r3.claim: Pausing after اليوم is stronger because otherwise the verse asserts that God has forgiven them, unless that assertion came by revelation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p278/r3.anchor: لأن الآخر فيه حكم على مغفرة الله، اللهم إلا أن يكون ذلك بوحي

MUQATIL:12:91-95/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:91-95/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:91-95/r2.claim: Joseph does not reproach his brothers for their misdeeds and asks God to forgive them; God is the most merciful.
MUQATIL:12:91-95/r2.anchor: { قال } يوسف: { لا تثريب عليكم اليوم } ، يقول: لا تعيير عليكم، لم يثرب عليهم بفعلهم القبيح،

ZAJJAJ:v3p128/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p128/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p128/r3.claim: Lā tathrība ʿalaykum means there is no reproach or harm upon you.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:90-92/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:90-92/r10.speaker: سفيان الثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:12:90-92/r10.claim: No reproach means no blaming, rebuking, or censure today; Sufyān al-Thawrī and others give this gloss, with al-yawm meaning the present time.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:90-92/r10.anchor: والتثريب التعيير والتوبيخ، أي لا تعيير ولا توبيخ ولا لوم عليكم اليوم قاله سفيان الثوري

ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.claim: Unlike Genesis' romantic account of Joseph's fortunes, the Qur'anic story illustrates God's unfathomable direction of human affairs: people may hate what is good for them or love what is bad for them.
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.anchor: the Qur'an uses it primarily as an illustration of God's unfathomable direction of men's affairs

TABATABAI:12:89-92/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:89-92/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:89-92/r6.claim: Tathrib means reproach, excessive blame, and enumerating sins; limiting the pardon to today highlights Joseph’s magnanimous restraint when his brothers stand powerless before him.
TABATABAI:12:89-92/r6.anchor: التثريب التوبيخ والمبالغة في اللوم وتعديد الذنوب

TABATABAI:12:89-92/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:89-92/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:89-92/r7.claim: Joseph then prays for forgiveness for all the brothers who wronged him, although only some of them are present; a later statement supports their absence.

TABRISI:12:90-92/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:90-92/r6.speaker: ابن الأعرابي، أبو عبيدة، ثعلب، أبو مسلم
TABRISI:12:90-92/r6.claim: Tathrīb means reproach: Ibn al-Aʿrabi gives rebuking, Abu ʿUbayda derives it from corruption, Thaʿlab says counting another's sins, and Abu Muslim connects it to inner fat for emphatic blame.

TABRISI:12:90-92/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:90-92/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:90-92/r9.claim: In لا تثريب عليكم, تثريب is an indefinite singular noun built with لا; عليكم is not governed by it but supplies an understood predicate or description, and اليوم may attach in several ways.
TABRISI:12:90-92/r9.anchor: تثريب نكرة مفردة مبنية مع لا على الفتح ولا يجوز أن يتعلق عليكم به

TABRISI:12:90-92/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:90-92/r10.speaker: الأخفش
TABRISI:12:90-92/r10.claim: Al-Akhfash prefers attaching اليوم to the next clause, so the phrase means 'today God forgives you'; the same syntax applies to لا ريب فيه.
TABRISI:12:90-92/r10.anchor: وهذا اختيار الأخفش وهكذا الكلام في قوله

TABRISI:12:90-92#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:90-92#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:90-92#2/r6.claim: Yusuf promises no blame or reproach today and asks God to forgive their past sin, saying he will seek forgiveness for them.
TABRISI:12:90-92#2/r6.anchor: لا تعيير ولا توبيخ ولا تقريع عليكم الآن فيما فعلتم

THALABI:v5p254/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p254/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p254/r4.claim: Yusuf, being forbearing and guided, says there will be no blame or reproach and he will not recall their sin; تثريب originally means corruption and is Hijazi usage.
THALABI:v5p254/r4.anchor: لا تثريب عليكم اليوم لا تعيير ولا تأنيب عليكم، ولا أذكر لكم ذنبكم بعد اليوم

THALABI:v5p254/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p254/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p254/r5.claim: The Prophet's instruction about a slave woman who commits adultery uses لا يثرب to mean do not reproach her.
THALABI:v5p254/r5.anchor: إذا زنت أمة أحدكم فليجلدها الحد ولا يثرب عليها

THALABI:v5p254/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p254/r6.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v5p254/r6.claim: Ata transmits Ibn Abbas's report that at the conquest of Mecca the Prophet asked what the people expected and answered as Yusuf had: no blame today.
THALABI:v5p254/r6.anchor: عطاء عن ابن عباس قال: أخذ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعضادتي الباب يوم فتح مكة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:90-93/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:90-93/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:90-93/r4.claim: Joseph promises no reproach after that day, forgives them, and asks God to forgive them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:90-93/r4.anchor: لا تأنيب ولا تعيير عليكم بعد هذا اليوم

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r1.claim: Joseph identifies himself by recalling what his brothers did to him and Benjamin, fulfilling the revelation that he would later tell them of it when they did not recognize him (12:15).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r1.anchor: Kardeşlerinin yaptıklarını bir gün onlara kendileri (senin kim olduğunun) farkına varmadan mutlaka haber vereceksin

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r2.claim: His brothers admit their wrong and apologize, and Joseph tells them he forgives them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r2.anchor: Kardeşleri kusurlarını itiraf edip özür dilediler. O da onları bağışladığını bildirdi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r3.claim: Envy cannot block a blessing God has decreed; the Prophet prayed that no one can withhold what God gives, and the brothers ultimately acknowledge God favored Joseph over them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r3.anchor: İnsanların kıskanması, Allah’ın bir kimse için takdir etmiş olduğu nimeti engelleyemez

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r4.speaker: Resûlullah
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r4.claim: The Prophet’s prayer says no one can prevent what God grants, and no one can grant what God withholds.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r4.anchor: Senin verdiğine engel olacak yoktur. Senin engel olduğunu da verecek yoktur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r5.speaker: Ziyâ Paşa
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r5.claim: Ziya Pasha’s couplet says divine power eventually makes tyrants admit that God favored another over them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r5.anchor: Zalimlere bir gün dedirir kudret-i Mevlâ

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The verb for blame means reproaching someone for a blameworthy deed; sincere regret makes forgiveness from noble Joseph and, one may hope, God appropriate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: If someone accepts his mistake with true regret, a person as noble as Joseph (sws) is bound to forgive him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: Prophet Muḥammad (sws)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: At the conquest of Makkah, the Prophet used Joseph's words to release the Quraysh leaders who had been his enemies; they called him a courteous brother and son of a courteous brother.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: these words were also uttered by Prophet Muḥammad (sws) at the conquest of Makkah

BURSEVI:v4p204/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p204/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p204/r5.claim: “No reproach” derives from removing the fat covering the stomach; severe blame is like melting a noble person's body, and Ibn al-Shaykh likens it to tearing honor and face.
BURSEVI:v4p204/r5.anchor: وهو تفعيل من الثرب وهو الشحم الذي يغشى الكرش

BURSEVI:v4p204/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p204/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p204/r6.claim: “Today” may limit the absence of blame to that day, implying all other days too, or attach to God's forgiveness: Joseph waived his personal claim and their repentance leaves God to forgive.
BURSEVI:v4p204/r6.anchor: واليوم منصوب بالتثريب أي لا تثريب عليكم اليوم الذي هو مظنة التثريب

BURSEVI:v4p204/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p204/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v4p204/r7.claim: The inward reading says the brothers' first wrongdoing ultimately became the means of Joseph's elevation and kingship, so he prays for their forgiveness.
BURSEVI:v4p204/r7.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية أخبر بصنيعهم في البداية ولكنه كان سبب رفعة منزلته

BURSEVI:v4p207/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p207/r5.speaker: شيخي وسندي
BURSEVI:v4p207/r5.claim: The shaykh's analysis contrasts Joseph's immediate forgiveness, arising from gratitude for the blessings his brothers' crime led to, with Jacob's delayed prayer until a sincere divinely permitted intention arose.
BURSEVI:v4p207/r5.anchor: انبعث من غيب قلب يوسف النظر إلى ما نال إليه بسبب إخوته من النعماء والآلاء

ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r1.claim: تثريب means blame or reproach; its root is the thin fat on the inner body, and the form denotes removal, metaphorically likening blame that exposes faults to stripping away what gives the face its fullness and beauty.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r1.anchor: وأصله من الثرب وهو الشحم الرقيق في الجوف وعلى الكرش وصيغة التفعيل للسلب أي ازالة الثرب

ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r2.claim: The comparison joins the loss of fat and the loss of reputation: both bring deficiency after completeness and remove what gives beauty.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r2.anchor: فالجامع بينهما طريان النقص بعد الكمال وازالة ما به الكمال والجمال

ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r3.claim: The noun after لا is تثريب; عليكم is linked to an omitted predicate, and اليوم can modify that predicate or its adverbial phrase. Limiting the assurance to today does not imply reproach later, since Joseph's restraint at their first meeting makes later reproach still less likely.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r3.anchor: وليس التقييد به لافادة وقوع التثريب في غيره فانه عليه السلام اذا لم يثرب أول لقائه واشتعال ناره فبعده بطريق الاولى

ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r4.speaker: المرتضى
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r4.claim: Al-Murtada reads اليوم as standing for all time, like the cited poetic lines about today's reversal of fortune.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r4.anchor: وقال المرتضى : إن ( اليوم ) موضوع موضع الزمان كله كقوله : اليوم يرحمنا من كان يغبطنا

ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows اليوم to attach to تثريب; Abu Hayyan objects that عليكم intervenes between the verbal noun and its complement, and that this analysis would make the noun quasi-annexed and therefore declinable with tanwin.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r5.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري تعلقه بتثريب وتعقبه أبو حيان قائلا : لايجوز ذلك لأن التثريب مصدر

ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r6.claim: Abu al-Baqa also rejects attaching اليوم to تثريب, arguing that the resulting quasi-annexed noun would have to be declinable and take tanwin.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r6.anchor: وكذا منع ذلك أبو البقاء وعالمه بلزوم الاعراب والتنوين أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r7.claim: The objection based on tanwin is not universal: grammatical texts and the agreed wording of a hadith show quasi-annexed nouns without tanwin, though grammarians disagree whether such forms are built or merely unmarked for tanwin.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r7.anchor: واعترض بأن المصرح به في متون النحو بأن شبيه المضاف سمع فيه عدم التنوين نحو لا طالع جبلا

ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r8.speaker: الرضي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r8.claim: Al-Radi says an adverb following negation attaches to an omitted predicate, and that اليوم here is governed by عليكم, though the reverse analysis is also possible.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50#2/r8.anchor: وذكر الرضي أن الظرف بعد النفي لايتعلق بالمنفي بل بمحذوف وهو خبر وأن ( اليوم ) في الآية معمول ( عليكم )

ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r1.claim: Another parsing makes the omitted predicate ذاك and attaches اليوم to يغفر الله لكم.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r1.anchor: جوز أيضا كون الخبر ذاك و ( اليوم ) متعلقا بقوله : ( ( يغفر الله لكم

ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r2.speaker: المرتضى
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r2.claim: Some weaken al-Murtada's attachment of اليوم to the forgiveness clause on the ground that a prayer cannot govern what precedes it.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r2.anchor: ونقل عن المرتضى أنه قال في الدرر : قد ضعف هذا قوم من جهة أن الدعاء لاينصب ماقبله

ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r3.speaker: ابن المنير
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r3.claim: Ibn al-Munir argues that reading Joseph's words as certain news of forgiveness conflicts with the brothers' later request that Jacob seek forgiveness for them.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r3.anchor: وقال ابن المنير : لو كان متعلقا به لقطعوا بالمغفرة باخبار الصديق ولم يكن كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r4.claim: Alusi finds that objection unpersuasive: forgiveness in the sense of concealment from punishment occurs on Judgment Day, and knowing through a truthful report that forgiveness will occur does not make asking for it pointless.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r4.anchor: وتعقب بأنه لاطائل تحته لأن المغفرة وهي ستر الذنب يوم القيامة حتى لايؤاخذوا به

ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r5.claim: The brothers may have asked Jacob to forgive offenses against his own rights, and may not yet have believed Joseph was a prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r5.anchor: وقد يقال أيضا : إن الذي طلبوه من أبيهم مغفرة ما يتعلق به ويرجع إلى حقه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r6.claim: Alusi favors taking the clause as a supplication: most readers pause after اليوم, and al-Tabari and Ibn Ishaq also prefer a prayer rather than a declaration of certain forgiveness.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r6.anchor: أكثر القراء على الوقف على ( اليوم ) وهو ظاهر في عدم تعلقه بيغفر وهو اختيار الطبري وابن إسحاق

ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r7.claim: Those who read the words as a declaration say Joseph's forgiveness of the brothers entails that God will forgive them too, in keeping with God's promise to accept repentance.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51/r7.anchor: ذهب جمع أيضا إلى كونه خبرا والحكم بذلك مع أنه غيب قيل : لأنه عليه السلام صفح عن جريمتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v13p51#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51#2/r1.claim: All mercy shown by creatures comes from God; even when it benefits another, it also relieves the merciful person of spiritual distress. God alone forgives every scale of sin and accepts the penitent.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51#2/r1.anchor: فان كل من يرحم سواه جل وعلا

ALUSI-FULL:v13p51#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51#2/r2.claim: A report says Joseph's brothers were embarrassed to eat with him because of their past, and he replied that his standing in Egyptians' eyes was greater now that they knew he was Abraham's descendant and his brothers were present.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51#2/r2.anchor: ومن كرم يوسف عليه السلام ما روى أن أخوته أرسلوا اليه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p51#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51#2/r3.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the king wanted Joseph involved in everything except the king's household; Joseph answered that he had greater grounds for pride as the son of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p51#2/r3.anchor: وكذا ماأخرجه سعيد بن منصور وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وأبو الشيخ عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v13p80#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p80#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p80#2/r10.claim: Joseph's immediate pardon exemplifies generosity: a generous person forgives when able, and an apology is accepted among the noble.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p80#2/r10.anchor: وهذا من شرائط الكرم فالكريم إذا قدر عفا

ALUSI-FULL:v13p82/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p82/r1.speaker: شاه الكرماني
ALUSI-FULL:v13p82/r1.claim: Whoever sees people through God's decree does not dwell on their offense; Joseph excused his brothers because he understood how destiny unfolds.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p82/r1.anchor: من نظر إلى الخلق بعين الحق لم يعبأ بمخالفتهم ومن نظر اليهم بعينه أفنى أيامه بمخاصمتهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p274#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p274#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p274#2/r2.claim: Joseph is forbearing: he tells them there will be no reproach or reminder of their sin from that day onward, and asks God to forgive them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p274#2/r2.anchor: لا تعيير عليكم اليوم، ولا أذكر لكم ذنبكم بعد اليوم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p274#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p274#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p274#2/r3.claim: After identifying himself, Joseph asks after his father; when told Jacob lost his sight, he gives them his shirt.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p274#2/r3.anchor: فلما عرفهم يوسف نفسه سألهم عن أبيه، فقال: ما فعل أبي بعدي؟

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:92/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:92/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:92/r1.claim: Tathrib means reproach; its root is fat covering the stomach, removed like a skin, and it metaphorically describes censure that tears honor and drains dignity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:92/r1.anchor: لا تأنيب عليكم تفعيل من الثرب وهو الشحم الذي يغشى الكرش للإزالة

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:92/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:92/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:92/r2.claim: Today may modify “no reproach,” emphasizing that Joseph will not blame them even when blame is expected, much less on other days.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:92/r2.anchor: والمعنى لا أثربكم اليوم الذي هو مظنته فما ظنكم بسائر الأيام

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:92/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:92/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:92/r3.claim: Alternatively, today modifies God's forgiveness: Joseph pardoned their crime then, and they acknowledged it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:92/r3.anchor: لأنه صفح عن جريمتهم حينئذ واعترفوا بها

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:92/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:92/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:92/r4.claim: God forgives minor and major sins and graciously favors the repentant.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:92/r4.anchor: فإنه يغفر الصغائر والكبائر ويتفضل على التائب

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:92/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:92/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:92/r5.claim: A story illustrates Joseph's generosity: his brothers felt ashamed to visit after their past wrong, and he said their kinship made Egyptians honor them as Abraham's descendants.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:92/r5.anchor: سبحان من بلغ عبدا بيع بعشرين درهما ما بلغ

BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r4.claim: Joseph's “no reproach today” removes blame precisely when blame seems warranted, so there is all the more reason for no reproach later.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r4.anchor: وإن كان هذا الوقت مظنة اللوم والتأنيب , فإذا انتفى ذلك فيه فما الظن بما بعده

BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r5.claim: “Tathrīb” means reproaching someone by stripping away the covering of pardon; the root's associations include persistence, confinement, and destruction, its dominant tendency being ruin.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r5.anchor: والتثريب : التقرير بالذنب , فهو إزالة ما على الإنسان من ساتر العفو

BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r6.claim: Joseph prays that God forgive all their past and possible future lapses; the imperfect verb encourages sincere repentance and hope in the Most Merciful, especially for the penitent.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r6.anchor: ولعله عبر في هذا الدعاء بالمضارع إرشادا لهم إلى إخلاص التوبة , ورغبهم في ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r7.claim: The brothers reportedly felt embarrassed accepting Joseph's daily hospitality; he says Egyptian observers once saw him as a slave bought for twenty dirhams, but now esteem him because he is their brother and Abraham's descendant.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r7.anchor: روى أنهم أرسلوا إليه أنك لتدعونا إلى طعامك وكرامتك بكرة وعشيا ونحن نستحي

DURR-FULL:v4p578/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p578/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v4p578/r1.claim: At Mecca’s conquest, the Prophet forgave its people using Joseph’s words: no reproach today, may God forgive you, and He is most merciful.
DURR-FULL:v4p578/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما فتح مكة طاف بالبيت

DURR-FULL:v4p578/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p578/r2.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
DURR-FULL:v4p578/r2.claim: Requests are easier to make of the young than elders; Joseph pardoned immediately while Jacob promised to seek forgiveness later.
DURR-FULL:v4p578/r2.anchor: عن عطاء الخراساني - رضي الله عنه - قال: طلب الحوائج إلى الشباب أسهل منها إلى الشيوخ

DURR-FULL:v4p578/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p578/r3.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني
DURR-FULL:v4p578/r3.claim: Abu Imran said he had never heard of forgiveness like Joseph’s.
DURR-FULL:v4p578/r3.anchor: عن أبي عمران الجوني - رضي الله عنه - قال: أما والله ما سمعنا بعفو قط مثل عفو يوسف

DURR-FULL:v4p578/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p578/r4.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR-FULL:v4p578/r4.claim: Jacob wrote Egypt’s ruler recounting the family’s trials and pleading that Benjamin was no thief; Joseph wept on reading it and ordered his shirt sent to restore Jacob’s sight.
DURR-FULL:v4p578/r4.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه - رضي الله عنه - قال: لما كان من أمر إخوة يوسف ما كان كتب يعقوب إلى يوسف

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses لا تثريب عليكم as no reproach or blame.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r1.anchor: عن أبي يحيى ، عن مجاهد : لا تثريب عليكم اليوم قال : لا اباء

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r2.claim: Qatadah says Joseph did not broadcast or reproach their past deeds, showing himself forbearing.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قوله لا تثريب عليكم اليوم يغفر الله لكم . قال : لقوا رجلا حليما لم يبث

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq explains the phrase as no rebuke for what the brothers had done.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r3.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق ، قال : لا تثريب عليكم اليوم . اي : لا تانيب عليكم اليوم

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r4.speaker: سفيان
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r4.claim: Sufyan glosses the phrase as no taunting today.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r4.anchor: قال سفيان في قوله : لا تثريب عليكم اليوم . قال : لا تعيير عليكم اليوم

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r5.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r5.claim: Ata al-Khurasani says it is easier to ask a young person for help than an elder, as Joseph immediately pardoned while Jacob deferred asking forgiveness.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r5.anchor: عن عطاء الخراساني ، قال : طلب الحوائج إلى الشباب اسهل منها عند الشيوخ

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r6.speaker: ابنا عمران الجوني
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r6.claim: The two sons of Imran al-Jawni say they had never heard of pardon like Joseph’s, which he gave after his brothers confessed.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r6.anchor: سمعت ابنا عمران الجوني يقولان : اما والله ما سمعنا بعفو قط مثل عفو يوسف

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r7.speaker: مالك بن دينار
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r7.claim: Malik ibn Dinar recounts al-Hasan praising Joseph’s forgiveness as an example preserved in scripture for later people to follow.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r7.anchor: ثنا مالك بن دينار قال : ارسل رجل إلى عشرة من اهل البصرة انا فيهم والحسن

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r8.speaker: محمد بن إسماعيل
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r8.claim: Ibn Ismail says Joseph promised God’s forgiveness when the brothers acknowledged their sin.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2195/r8.anchor: عن محمد بن اسماعيل يغفر الله لكم وهو ارحم الراحمين . قال : حين اعترفوا بذنبهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p50/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p50/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p50/r1.claim: The added عليكم intensifies reassurance; today belongs with the promise to forgive, not the preceding clause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p50/r1.anchor: وزيادة عليكم } للتأكيد مثل زيادة { لك } بعد ( سقيا ورعيا ) ، فلا يكون قوله : { اليوم } من تمام الجملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p50/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p50/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p50/r2.claim: Joseph says God forgives them at this moment of repentance under prior revealed laws; revelation is needed only to know their repentance is sincere.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p50/r2.anchor: وأعقب ذلك بأن أعلمهم بأن الله يغفر لهم في تلك الساعة لأنها ساعة توبة ، فالذنب مغفور لإخبار الله في شرائعه السالفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p50/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p50/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p50/r3.claim: Today may denote a span of time; Ibn Ashur compares its use at 5:3.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p50/r3.anchor: وأطلق { اليوم } على الزمن ، وقد مضى عند قوله تعالى : { اليوم يئس الذين كفروا من دينكم في أول سورة العقود

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r1.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r1.claim: Joseph promises not to reproach his brothers for this ever again.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو صالح عن ابن عباس لا أعيركم بعد اليوم بهذا أبدا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r2.claim: Joseph specifies “today” because it is the first moment of pardon, when one who forgives should not revisit punishment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r2.anchor: إنما أشار إلى ذلك اليوم لأنه أول أوقات العفو وسبيل العافي في مثله أن لا يراجع عقوبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r3.speaker: ثعلب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r3.claim: The verb tharraba means to enumerate someone’s sins against them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r3.anchor: قد ثرب فلان على فلان إذا عدد عليه ذنوبه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r4.claim: He glosses the phrase as no blaming after that day and traces taṯrīb to corruption or spoiling.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r4.anchor: لا تعيير عليكم بعد هذا اليوم بما صنعتم وأصل التثريب الإفساد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r5.claim: A hadith instructs that if a slave woman commits adultery she is to be flogged, but not reproached afterward.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث إذا زنت أمة أحدكم فليجلدها الحد ولا يثرب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r6.claim: Joseph absolved them and asked God to forgive them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282#2/r6.anchor: جعلهم في حل وسأل الله المغفرة لهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p408#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p408#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p408#2/r1.claim: Joseph says there will be no blame, reproach, or renewed mention of their sin against him from that day onward.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p408#2/r1.anchor: {قال لا تثريب عليكم اليوم} يقول: لا تأنيب عليكم ولا عتب عليكم اليوم، ولا أعيد (7) ذنبكم في حقي بعد اليوم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p408#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p408#2/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p408#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says the brothers apologized and Joseph answered that he would not mention their sin.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p408#2/r2.anchor: قال السدي: اعتذروا إلى يوسف، فقال: {لا تثريب عليكم اليوم} يقول: لا أذكر لكم ذنبكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p408#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p408#2/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق والثوري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p408#2/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq and al-Thawri interpret the words as no rebuke from Joseph that day, with God covering and forgiving what they did.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p408#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق والثوري: {لا تثريب عليكم [اليوم] } (1) أي: لا تأنيب عليكم اليوم عندي فيما صنعتم {يغفر الله لكم} أي: يستر الله عليكم فيما فعلتم

JISHUMI:v5p3709/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3709/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3709/r12.claim: ثرب and تثريب concern blame, damage, and enumerating someone's sins; ثرب also names thin abdominal fat, with سماحيق الشحم as a comparison in a hadith gloss.
JISHUMI:v5p3709/r12.anchor: والثرب: اللوم والإفساد والتقرير بالذنب، والثرب: الشحمة الرقيقة في الجوف، وجمعها: ثروب،

JISHUMI:v5p3709/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3709/r13.speaker: أبو عبيدة
JISHUMI:v5p3709/r13.claim: Abu Ubayda derives ثرب from فساد, corruption.
JISHUMI:v5p3709/r13.anchor: وقيل: أصله الإفساد، عن أبي عبيدة، قال الشاعر:

JISHUMI:v5p3709/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3709/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3709/r14.claim: A poetic line uses غير مثرب for pardon without reproach or blame.
JISHUMI:v5p3709/r14.anchor: قال الشاعر: فعفوت عنهم عفو غير مثرب ... وتركتهم لعقاب يوم سرمد

JISHUMI:v5p3709/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3709/r15.speaker: ثعلب
JISHUMI:v5p3709/r15.claim: Thaʿlab says ثرب على someone means listing that person's sins against them.
JISHUMI:v5p3709/r15.anchor: قال ثعلب: يقال: ثرب فلان على فلان إذا عدد عليه ذنوبه

JISHUMI:v5p3709/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3709/r16.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v5p3709/r16.claim: Abu Muslim derives تثريب from body fat, making it an intensified form of blame and reproach carried to its furthest extent.
JISHUMI:v5p3709/r16.anchor: قال أبو مسلم: التثريب مأخوذ من الثرب، وهو شحم الجوف، فكأنه موضوع للمبالغة في اللوم والتعنيف،

JISHUMI:v5p3710/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r2.claim: لا تثريب is accusative as a verbal noun; اليوم can be accusative as an adverb under negation or nominative by construing the clause as ليس بتثريب.
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r2.anchor: ونصب لا تثريب على التثربة، و(اليوم) نصب على الظرف، ويجوز فيه الرفع

JISHUMI:v5p3710/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r9.speaker: سفيان، وأبو علي
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r9.claim: One gloss of لا تثريب عليكم اليوم is that Joseph will neither investigate nor rebuke them.
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r9.anchor: قال يوسف لا تثريب عليكم اليوم قيل: لا تفتيش ولا توبيخ، عن سفيان، وأبي علي،

JISHUMI:v5p3710/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r10.speaker: أبو عبيدة، وأبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r10.claim: Another gloss says there will be no punishment or harm that spoils their situation.
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r10.anchor: وقيل: لا معاقبة ولا إفساد، عن أبي عبيدة، وأبي مسلم، يعني لا يلحقكم مني ما يفسد حالكم،

JISHUMI:v5p3710/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r11.claim: Other explanations of لا تثريب are no recounting of sins or no blame at all.
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r11.anchor: وقيل: لا تعداد للذنوب، وقيل: لا لوم عليكم، اليوم يرفع اللوم،

JISHUMI:v5p3710/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r12.claim: Today may mark the first moment Joseph revealed himself, when revenge was possible; alternatively it ends the earlier rebuke he gave while they did not know him, or means the whole span of time.
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r12.anchor: قيل: لأنه أول أوقاته التي كشف فيها نفسه لهم، فكان وقت الانتقام، فمتى عفا لم يرجع،

JISHUMI:v5p3710/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r13.claim: The word اليوم may instead begin a new clause, so the pause comes after لا تثريب عليكم.
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r13.anchor: وقيل: تم الكلام عند قوله: (لا تثريب عليكم) ثم ابتدأ بقوله: اليوم يغفر الله لكم

JISHUMI:v5p3710/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r14.claim: يغفر الله لكم may be Joseph's prayer for them, or a respectful statement that God is entitled to His due and may forgive them.
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r14.anchor: يغفر الله لكم قيل هو دعاء لهم، وقيل: لما كان الله تعالى آخذا لحقه منهم

AKHFASH:v1p399#3/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p399#3/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p399#3/r2.claim: Pause after اليوم; then يغفر الله لكم begins a new sentence and functions as a fresh prayer for forgiveness.
AKHFASH:v1p399#3/r2.anchor: وقال {لا تثريب عليكم اليوم} (اليوم) وقف ثم استأنف فقال {يغفر الله لكم}

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r3.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r3.claim: “No reproach on you” can mean no blame or alteration is laid on them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r3.anchor: لا تغيير عليكم , وهو قول سفيان ابن عيينة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r4.claim: It can mean no reproach for what they did.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r4.anchor: لا تأنيب فيما صنعتم , قاله ابن إسحاق

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r5.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r5.claim: It may mean Joseph has no aversion to what they said.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r5.anchor: لا إباء عليكم في قولكم , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r6.claim: A fourth gloss is that there will be no punishment.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r7.claim: God's forgiveness may follow their repentance, confession, and regret.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r8.claim: Alternatively, God forgives because Joseph has made pardon permissible for them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r9.claim: “He is the most merciful” may refer to God's making Joseph a king.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r9.anchor: في صنعه بي حين جعلني ملكا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r10.claim: Alternatively, it refers to God's mercy in pardoning the brothers' earlier offense.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r10.anchor: في عفوه عنكم عما تقدم من ذنبكم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p222#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p222#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p222#3/r1.claim: There will be no reproach after this day; the root of tathrīb is causing corruption or spoiling, as in the idiom tharraba ʿalaynā.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p222#3/r1.anchor: {قال لا تثريب عليكم اليوم} لا تعيير عليكم بعد هذا اليوم بما صنعتم. وأصل التثريب: الإفساد.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p222#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p222#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p222#3/r2.claim: A hadith says to apply the prescribed penalty to an enslaved woman who commits adultery but not to reproach her for it.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p222#3/r2.anchor: وفي الحديث: "إذا زنت أمة أحدكم: فليجلدها الحد، ولا يثرب".

NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r1.claim: Tathrīb means reproach or blame; Joseph's expression can link “today” either to reproach or to God's forgiveness.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r1.anchor: لا تعيير عليكم ﴿ اليوم ﴾ متعلق بالتثريب أو بيغفر

NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r2.claim: The meaning may be that there is no blame today, the day most suited to blame; this implies still more that there is none on other days.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r2.anchor: وهو اليوم الذي هو مظنة التثريب فما ظنكم بغيره من الأيام

NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r3.claim: Alternatively, Joseph begins a new sentence with a prayer that God forgive what they did; the past and present forms of the forgiveness formula are both used.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r3.anchor: ثم ابتدأ فقال ﴿ يغفر الله لكم ﴾ فدعا لهم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r4.claim: “Today God forgives you” can be understood as glad tidings of forgiveness arriving soon.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r4.anchor: اليوم يغفر الله لكم بشارة بعاجل غفران الله

NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r5.claim: At the conquest of Mecca, the Prophet asked Quraysh what they thought he would do; they expected kindness from a noble kinsman, and he answered with Joseph's words, “No reproach upon you today.”
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r5.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أخذ بعضادتى باب الكعبة يوم الفتح

NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r6.speaker: العباس
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r6.claim: When Abu Sufyan came to become Muslim, al-Abbas told him to recite Joseph's words to the Prophet; the Prophet then prayed that God forgive Abu Sufyan and the person who taught him.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r6.anchor: أن أبا سفيان لما جاء ليسلم قال له العباس إذا أتيت رسول الله فاتل عليه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r7.claim: The brothers reportedly felt ashamed to accept Joseph's daily hospitality after their past actions; he said his Egyptian subjects had once seen him as a slave sold for twenty dirhams, but now his honor came through being known as Abraham's descendants.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r7.anchor: إنك تدعونا إلى طعامك بكرة وعشيا ونحن نستحى منك لما فرط منا فيك

NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r8.claim: Joseph reasons that if he, a poor and miserly person, is merciful to them, they should consider how much more merciful the rich, forgiving God is.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#4/r8.anchor: إذا رحمتكم وأنا الفقير القتور فما ظنكم بالغنى الغفور

QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r1.claim: Tathrīb means reproaching or shaming someone; a report about punishing a slave girl instructs the owner not to reproach her afterward.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r1.anchor:
أي لا يعيرها وقال بشر:
فعفوت عنهم عفو غير مثرب

QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r2.speaker: بشر
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r2.claim: The poet Bishr uses mutathrib for one who reproaches.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r2.anchor:
وقال بشر:
فعفوت عنهم عفو غير مثرب
وتركتهم لعقاب يوم سرمد

QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r3.speaker: الأصمعي
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r3.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī says tathrīb and taʿrīb both mean blaming someone for an act.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r3.anchor: وقال الأصمعي: ثربت عليه وعربت عليه بمعنى إذا قبحت عليه فعله

QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r4.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj interprets the phrase as preserving the bond of kinship and offering pardon; the root means corruption in Hijazi speech.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج: المعنى لا إفساد لما بيني وبينكم من الحرمة، وحق الإخوة، ولكم عندي العفو والصفح وأصل التثريب الإفساد

QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that at Mecca’s conquest the Prophet invoked Joseph’s words of pardon to Quraysh; ʿUmar felt ashamed because he had proposed revenge.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r5.anchor:
وعن ابن عباس
" أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أخذ بعضادتي الباب يوم فتح مكة

QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r6.claim: The verb “God will forgive you” is formally future but functions as a prayer asking God to conceal and show mercy.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r6.anchor: يغفر الله لكم } مستقبل فيه معنى الدعاء سأل الله أن يستر عليهم ويرحمهم

QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r7.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r7.claim: Al-Akhfash allows a pause after “upon you,” reading “today” with the following prayer.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r8.claim: The author prefers joining the phrase, since pausing would assert certain forgiveness that day, something possible only through revelation.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r8.anchor: والأول هو المستعمل فإن في الوقف على «عليكم» والابتداء ب «اليوم يغفر الله لكم» جزم

QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r9.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r9.claim: ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī says it is easier to ask young people for needs than old people, contrasting Joseph’s immediate forgiveness with Jacob’s later prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:92-93/r9.anchor: وقال عطاء الخراساني: طلب الحوائج من الشباب أسهل منه من الشيوخ ألم تر قول يوسف

MAJAZ:v1p317/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p317/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p317/r5.claim: لا تثريب عليكم means no reproach, confusion, clamor, corruption, or punishment.
MAJAZ:v1p317/r5.anchor: «لا تثريب عليكم اليوم» (92) أي لا تخليط ولا شغب ولا إفساد ولا معاقبة

RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r1.claim: Joseph answers the brothers’ confession and admission of guilt by removing blame and reproach from them.
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r1.anchor: لما اعترفوا بفضله عليهم وبكونهم مجرمين خاطئين قال يوسف

RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r2.claim: Tathrīb means reproach or fault-finding; its root is tharb, the fat covering the stomach, and the verb suggests removing it.
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r2.anchor: أي لا توبيخ ولا عيب وأصل التثريب من الثرب

RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r3.speaker: الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r3.claim: A Prophetic report says that after an enslaved woman receives the prescribed punishment, she must not be taunted for fornication.
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r3.anchor: قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( إذا زنت أمة أحدكم فليضربها الحد

RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r4.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r4.claim: It is easier to ask young people for help than elders, as Joseph absolves his brothers while Jacob says he will seek forgiveness.
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r4.anchor: قال عطاء الخراساني طلب الحوائج إلى الشباب أسهل منها إلى الشيوخ

RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r5.claim: One reading connects today to the denial of reproach: if there is no reproach on this especially blameworthy day, there will be none on other days.
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r5.anchor: إنه متعلق بقوله : { لا تثريب } أي لا أثر بكم اليوم

RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r6.claim: Alternatively, today marks Joseph’s present ruling of universal absolution: denying reproach as a kind denies every instance across times and circumstances.
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r6.anchor: نفي للماهية ونفي الماهية يقتضي انتفاء جميع أفراد الماهية

RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r7.claim: Joseph then asks God to remove their punishment in the afterlife; God forgive you is a supplication.
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r7.anchor: لما بين لهم أنه أزال عنهم ملامة الدنيا طلب من الله أن يزيل عنهم عقاب الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r8.claim: Another reading connects today to forgiveness: God accepted their repentance and forgave them that day after their shame, confession, and return.
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r8.anchor: لما انكسروا وخجلوا واعترفوا وتابوا فالله قبل توبتهم وغفر ذنبهم

RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r9.speaker: الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r9.claim: At the conquest of Mecca, the Prophet asked Quraysh what they thought he would do and answered with Joseph’s words of absolution.
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r9.anchor: الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام أخذ بعضادتي باب الكعبة يوم الفتح

RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r10.speaker: العباس
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r10.claim: Abbas told Abu Sufyan to recite Joseph’s words when approaching the Prophet; the Prophet prayed that God forgive Abu Sufyan and his teacher.
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r10.anchor: أن أبا سفيان لما جاء ليسلم قال له العباس

RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r11.speaker: يوسف عليه السلام
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r11.claim: When his brothers felt ashamed to dine with him because of their past mistreatment, Joseph said their visit now honored him and made Egyptians recognize his kinship to Abraham.
RAZI-FULL:v18p164/r11.anchor: إن أهل مصر وإن ملكت فيهم فإنهم ينظروني بالعين الأولى

STUDYQURAN:12:91/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:91/r1.speaker: Kl
STUDYQURAN:12:91/r1.claim: Joseph’s no-reproach statement is called a beautiful form of forgiveness; reproach may also mean physical punishment.
STUDYQURAN:12:91/r1.anchor: There is no reproach against you this day is described in some sources as “a beautiful form of forgiveness”(Kl)

STUDYQURAN:12:91/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:91/r2.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
STUDYQURAN:12:91/r2.claim: At the conquest of Mecca, the Prophet cited Joseph’s forgiveness, then freed Quraysh after they acknowledged his noble status.
STUDYQURAN:12:91/r2.anchor: “Verily I say to you as Joseph said to his brothers: there is no reproach against you

TAB-FULL:v13p330/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p330/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p330/r1.claim: Joseph promises no reproach, alteration, or damage to the bond and rights of brotherhood; he instead grants pardon and forgiveness.
TAB-FULL:v13p330/r1.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق: {قال لا تثريب عليكم اليوم} [يوسف: 92] «لا تأنيب عليكم اليوم عندي فيما صنعتم»

TAB-FULL:v13p330/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p330/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p330/r2.claim: Joseph did not reproach his brothers for their deeds.
TAB-FULL:v13p330/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {لا تثريب عليكم} [يوسف: 92] لم يثرب عليهم أعمالهم

TAB-FULL:v13p330/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p330/r3.speaker: سفيان
TAB-FULL:v13p330/r3.claim: لا تثريب means there will be no change in their relationship.

TAB-FULL:v13p330/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p330/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v13p330/r4.claim: Joseph tells them he will not blame them before him for what they did.
TAB-FULL:v13p330/r4.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق: {قال لا تثريب عليكم اليوم} [يوسف: 92] «لا تأنيب عليكم اليوم عندي فيما صنعتم»

TAB-FULL:v13p330/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p330/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v13p330/r5.claim: Joseph says he will not bring up their sin to them.
TAB-FULL:v13p330/r5.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " اعتذروا إلى يوسف، فقال: {لا تثريب عليكم اليوم} [يوسف: 92] يقول: «لا أذكر لكم ذنبكم»

TAB-FULL:v13p330/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p330/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p330/r6.claim: Joseph’s words asking God to forgive them are a supplication that He pardon and conceal their wrong against him.
TAB-FULL:v13p330/r6.anchor: وهذا دعاء من يوسف لإخوته بأن يغفر الله لهم ذنبهم فيما أتوا إليه، وركبوا منه من الظلم، يقول: عفا الله لكم عن ذنبكم وظلمكم، فستره عليكم؛

TAB-FULL:v13p330/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p330/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p330/r7.claim: God is most merciful to those who repent from sin and return to obedience.
TAB-FULL:v13p330/r7.anchor: يقول: والله أرحم الراحمين لمن تاب من ذنبه، وأناب إلى طاعته بالتوبة من معصيته، كما

TAB-FULL:v13p330/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p330/r8.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v13p330/r8.claim: Joseph asks forgiveness for them after they acknowledge their sin.
TAB-FULL:v13p330/r8.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق: {يغفر الله لكم وهو أرحم الراحمين} [يوسف: 92] حيث اعترفوا بذنبهم

TABRISI:12:92-93/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:92-93/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:92-93/r1.claim: One interpretation connects Joseph's pardon with God's treatment of him that made him king.
TABRISI:12:92-93/r1.anchor: وقيل: في صنيعه بي حتى جعلني ملكا

TABRISI:12:92-93/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:92-93/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:92-93/r2.claim: Al-yawm can mean an entire period; the cited poem contrasts people who now pity with those once followed.
TABRISI:12:92-93/r2.anchor: وقيل: أراد باليوم الزمان فتدخل فيه الأوقات كلها كما قال الشاعر

TABRISI:12:92-93/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:92-93/r3.speaker: الشاعر
TABRISI:12:92-93/r3.claim: The cited line uses al-yawm for an extended period.
TABRISI:12:92-93/r3.anchor: فاليوم يرحمنا من كان يغبطنا واليوم نتبع من كانوا لنا تبعا

TABRISI:12:92-93/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:92-93/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:92-93/r4.claim: Alternatively the speech ends at no reproach upon you; today God forgives you begins as a prayer.
TABRISI:12:92-93/r4.anchor: وقيل: إن الكلام قد تم عند قوله { لا تثريب عليكم } ثم ابتدأ بقوله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p237/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p237/r1.speaker: ثعلب عن ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p237/r1.claim: ثرب means to rebuke or reproach; the root has variants ثرب and أثرب.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p237/r1.anchor: روى ثعلب عن ابن الأعرابي (¬1): الثارب الموبخ، يقال: ثرب، وثرب، وأثرب إذا وبخ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p237/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p237/r2.speaker: الحديث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p237/r2.claim: A hadith says to punish an enslaved woman for adultery without reproaching her about it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p237/r2.anchor: إذا زنت أمة أحدكم فليضربها الحد ولا يثربها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p237/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p237/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p237/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj glosses the phrase as no harm or corruption.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p237/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج (¬3): معناه: لا إفساد عليكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p237/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p237/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p237/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda expands it as no disturbance, punishment, or corruption and cites a poem about pardoning without reproach.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p237/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة (¬4): معناه: لا شغب ولا معاقبة ولا إفساد، وأنشد (¬5):

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r1.speaker: أبو العباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r1.claim: To reproach someone can mean to enumerate that person's sins.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r1.anchor: وروى ابن الأنباري عن أبي العباس (¬1): ثرب فلان على فلان، إذا عدد عليه ذنوبه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومحمد بن إسحاق وسفيان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r2.claim: They explain the phrase as no blame, no reprimand, or no taunting.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد لا لوم عليكم، وقال محمد بن إسحاق (¬2): لا (¬3) تأنيب عليكم، وقال سفيان (¬4): لا تعيير عليكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r3.claim: He makes Joseph promise never again to taunt them with this deed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r3.anchor: وقال الكلبي (¬5): يقول لا أعيركم بعد اليوم بهذا أبدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r4.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r4.claim: Because Joseph had reproached them before revealing himself, اليوم marks the end of reproach after their confession and implies the same pardon in later days; today can mean a period generally.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r4.anchor: قال أبو بكر (¬6): إن يوسف لما قدم توبيخهم، وعدد عليهم قبيح ما فعلوا، وهو يستر عنهم نفسه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r5.speaker: امرؤ القيس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r5.claim: His line using اليوم shows that the word can mean a time or period, rather than a particular day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r5.anchor: كقول امرئ القيس: فاليوم أشرب غير مستحقب ... إثما من الله ولا واغل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r6.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r6.claim: A weaker alternative attaches اليوم to the prayer that God forgive them today; he notes the syntactic objection that a prayer is not governed beforehand, but allows it because يغفر is indicative, as al-Akhfash permits pausing after عليكم.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p238/r6.anchor: قال أبو بكر (¬6): إن يوسف لما قدم توبيخهم، وعدد عليهم قبيح ما فعلوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p239/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p239/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p239/r1.claim: Joseph put his brothers wholly at ease, asked God to forgive them, and said God is more merciful to His devoted servants than parents are to children.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p239/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬2): جعلهم في كل حل، وسأل الله لهم المغفرة، وأخبر أن الله أرحم بأوليائه

SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r1.claim: ‘عليكم’ may be the predicate of لا, with ‘اليوم’ linked to it: no reproach is settled upon you today.
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r1.anchor: " عليكم " يجوز أن يكون خبرا ل " لا " ، و " اليوم "

SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r2.claim: Alternatively, ‘اليوم’ is the predicate of لا and ‘عليكم’ attaches to the implicit predication in the adverb.
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون " اليوم " خبر " لا " و " عليكم " متعلق بما تعلق به هذا الظرف

SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r3.claim: A third parse makes ‘عليكم’ an adjective of لا’s noun and ‘اليوم’ its predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون " عليكم " صفة لاسم " لا " ، و " اليوم " خبرها أيضا

SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r4.claim: He rejects attaching both modifiers directly to ‘تثريب’: the noun would resemble an annexation but stay indefinite, and the order would separate a source phrase from its complement with an intervening constituent.
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r4.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يتعلق كل من الظرف والجار ب " تثريب " لأنه يصير مطولا شبيها بالمضاف

SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows ‘اليوم’ to modify ‘تثريب’, the implicit stability in ‘عليكم’, or ‘يغفر’; the author says the first option has the preceding syntactic problem.
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r5.anchor: وقد جوز الزمخشري أن يكون الظرف متعلقا ب " تثريب " فقال: " فإن قلت: بم يتعلق " اليوم "؟ قلت: بالتثريب

SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r6.speaker: الفارسي
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r6.claim: Al-Fārisī cites a poetic use where ‘كفران’ governs ‘أية’ despite its suppressed nun, treating the noun like an annex; an implicit ‘أويت’ is rejected because it would split أرى’s two objects with two clauses.
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r6.anchor: وجعل الفارسي من ذلك قوله: 2830 أراني ولا كفران لله أية

SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r7.speaker: جمال الدين بن مالك
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r7.claim: Ibn Mālik analyzes ‘لا صمت يوم إلى الليل’ with nominative ‘يوم’ governed by a verbal noun understood as a passive verb plus مصدرية particle; the source leaves disagreement aside.
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r7.anchor: وجعل منه الشيخ جمال الدين بن مالك ما جاء في الحديث " لا صمت يوم إلى الليل "

SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r8.claim: Attaching ‘اليوم’ to the implicit stability in ‘عليكم’ is clear and explains why most readers pause after ‘عليكم’ before ‘يغفر الله لكم’.
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r8.anchor: وأما تعليقه بالاستقرار المقدر فواضح، ولذلك وقف أكثر القراء عليه، وابتدأ ب { يغفر الله لكم }

SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r9.claim: Attaching ‘اليوم’ to ‘يغفر’ is also clear and explains why some readers pause after ‘عليكم’ and begin ‘اليوم يغفر الله لكم’.
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r9.anchor: وأما تعليقه ب " يغفر " فواضح أيضا ولذلك وقف بعض القراء على " عليكم "

SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r10.claim: ‘عليكم’ may be an explanatory complement like ‘لك’ in ‘سقيا لك’; another option omits لا’s predicate and links ‘عليكم’ and ‘اليوم’ to an implied verb indicated by ‘تثريب’.
SAMIN-DURR:12:92/r10.anchor: وجوزوا أن يكون " عليكم " بيانا ك " لك " في نحو " سقيا لك "

SAMIN-DURR:12:92#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:92#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:92#2/r1.claim: A proposed ellipsis supplies ‘لا تثريب يثرب عليكم اليوم’, parallel to the implied verb in ‘لا عاصم اليوم من أمر الله’ (11:43); the Shaykh says this analysis would be strong.
SAMIN-DURR:12:92#2/r1.anchor: لا عاصم اليوم من أمر الله [هود: 43] لا عاصم يعصم اليوم. قال الشيخ: " لو قيل به لكان قويا "

SAMIN-DURR:12:92#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:92#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:92#2/r2.claim: He distinguishes the ellipses: the ‘تثريب’ analysis deletes two elements and makes the verb metaphorical, whereas ‘عاصم يعصم’ needs one deletion and is literal.
SAMIN-DURR:12:92#2/r2.anchor: وقد يفرق بينهما بأن هنا يلزم كثرة المجاز، وذلك أنك تحذف الخبر، وتحذف هذا الذي تعلق به الظرف

SAMIN-DURR:12:92#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:92#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:92#2/r3.claim: ‘التثريب’ means reproach, rebuke, or shaming; in a hadith, ‘ولا يثرب’ means not to reproach or taunt.
SAMIN-DURR:12:92#2/r3.anchor: والتثريب العتب والتأنيب، وعبر بعضهم عنه بالتعيير، من عيرته بكذا إذا عبته به

SAMIN-DURR:12:92#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:92#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:92#2/r4.claim: The word derives from ‘الثرب’, thin fat covering the stomach: reproach figuratively strips this covering, an image for tearing at someone’s reputation.
SAMIN-DURR:12:92#2/r4.anchor: وأصله من الثرب وهو ما يغشى الكرش من الشحم، ومعناه إزالة الثرب كما أن التجليد

SAMIN-DURR:12:92#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:92#2/r5.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:12:92#2/r5.claim: Al-Rāghib says the known lexical form is ‘الثرب’, a thin piece of fat, and suggests ‘يثرب’ (33:13) may come from the same root with an added yāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:12:92#2/r5.anchor: وقال الراغب: " ولا يعرف من لفظه إلا قولهم " الثرب " وهو شحمة رقيقة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p317/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p317/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p317/r1.claim: تثريب means removing reproach; the word derives from fat surrounding the stomach, and rebuke figuratively strips honor and beauty.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p317/r1.anchor: وأصله من الثرب وهو الشحم الذي هو غاشية الكرش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p317/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p317/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p317/r2.claim: فند means corruption; the cited poetry illustrates the term and its verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p317/r2.anchor:
الفند: الفساد، قال:
ألا سليمان إذ قال الإله له

BURHAN:v3p347/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p347/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p347/r4.claim: Joseph’s “no reproach upon you today” is included among reports used in place of a request or command.

BURHAN:v4p350/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p350/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p350/r4.claim: The negative lā may govern like inna and negate an entire genus; lā tathrība ʿalaykum is one example, often with its understood predicate omitted.
BURHAN:v4p350/r4.anchor: فالداخلة على الأسماء تكون عاملة وغير عاملة فالعاملة قسمان تارة تعمل عمل إن وهي النافية للجنس

BURHAN:v4p350/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p350/r5.speaker: الزمخشري والحريري
BURHAN:v4p350/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī and al-Ḥarīrī say the non-governing lā only denies one instance; al-Zarkashī rejects their restriction and notes that negation can intend the whole genus.
BURHAN:v4p350/r5.anchor: وزعم الزمخشري في المفصل أنها غير عاملة وكذا قال الحريري في الدرة إنها لا تأتي إلا لنفي الوحدة

BURHAN:v4p350/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p350/r8.speaker: ابن الحاجب
BURHAN:v4p350/r8.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib says al-Zamakhsharī's claim fails: grammarians agree that an indefinite noun under negation yields generality, though the built form on fatḥa signals it more strongly.
BURHAN:v4p350/r8.anchor: وقال ابن الحاجب ما قاله الزمخشري لا يستقيم ولا خلاف عند أصحاب الفهم انه يستفاد العموم منه

ITQAN:v3p105/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p105/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p105/r5.claim: Joseph’s declarative ‘God forgives you’ is a prayer meaning ‘May God forgive you.’
ITQAN:v3p105/r5.anchor: ﴿ لا تثريب عليكم اليوم يغفر الله لكم ﴾ أي اللهم اغفر لهم

ITQAN:v2p529/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p529/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p529/r3.claim: In lā ʿāṣim al-yawm and lā tathrīb ʿalaykum al-yawm, al-yawm cannot modify the noun of lā, which would then require accusative nunation; it modifies an omitted element.
ITQAN:v2p529/r3.anchor: إن اسم لا حينئذ مطول فيجب نصبه وتنوينه وإنما هو متعلق بمحذوف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p698/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p698/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p698/r2.claim: Joseph’s brothers did not ask him to forgive them or name their offense, using a light إن; to their father they explicitly requested forgiveness and admitted their sins emphatically with إنّا.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p698/r2.anchor: هم لم يسألوه المغفرة وإنما هو الذي دعا لهم بالمغفرة دون أن يسألوه حتى أنهم لم يذكروا الخطيئة التي ارتكبوها بحق يوسف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p698/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p698/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p698/r3.claim: Jacob promises delayed intercession because his sons’ deed caused him greater lasting suffering, including blindness and grief; unlike Joseph, he had not ceased to feel its pain.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p698/r3.anchor: أما تأثير فعلة إخوة يوسف على أبيهم فكان أعظم لأنه أصيب بالعمى والأسى والحسرة على ولده

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p699/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p699/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p699/r1.claim: Joseph immediately absolves his brothers and asks God to forgive them because their act ultimately benefited him.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p699/r1.anchor: لأنه استفاد من فعلة إخوته معه

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p188/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p188/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p188/r4.claim: In لا تثريب عليكم اليوم, neither عليكم nor اليوم can complete the verbal noun تثريب, since a source cannot be built as a single negative noun before its complements are complete.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p188/r4.anchor: فأما قوله: لا تثريب عليكم اليوم [يوسف/ 92] فلا يخلو قوله

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p188/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p188/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p188/r5.claim: After rejecting attachment to تثريب, عليكم can modify the indefinite verbal noun through an implied element and اليوم can serve as its temporal predicate.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p188/r5.anchor: فإذا لم يجز تعلقهما ولا تعلق واحد منهما بالمصدر تعلق بغيرهما

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p191/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p191/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p191/r1.claim: For لا تثريب عليكم اليوم, اليوم may modify the implied adjective of عليكم; both require an omitted predicate, or اليوم may be a ظرف of عليكم with the same ellipsis.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p191/r1.anchor: ويجوز أيضا أن يكون (اليوم) متعلقا بما هو في موضع صفة، كما كان (عليكم) كذلك

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p191/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p191/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p191/r2.claim: A further parse makes اليوم govern عليكم while عليكم itself is the predicate, requiring no separate adjective analysis.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p191/r2.anchor: ويجوز أيضا أن يتعلق اليوم بعليكم على أن يكون (عليكم) خبرا لا صفة

AZRAQI:v2p121/r1.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p121/r1.speaker: النبي
AZRAQI:v2p121/r1.claim: On the conquest day, after praying two rakʿahs in the Kaaba, the Prophet asks Quraysh what they expect; when they appeal to his generosity, he quotes Joseph's pardon and asks God to forgive them.
AZRAQI:v2p121/r1.anchor: عن عطاء بن أبي رباح والحسن بن أبي الحسن وطاوس أن النبي & دخل يوم الفتح البيت فصلى فيه ركعتين

AZRAQI:v2p121/r2.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p121/r2.speaker: النبي
AZRAQI:v2p121/r2.claim: The Prophet abolishes pre-Islamic claims for usury, blood, and property, while preserving the Kaaba's custodianship and pilgrims' water service for their current holders.
AZRAQI:v2p121/r2.anchor: لا أن كل ربا كان في الجاهلية أو دم أو مال فهو تحت قديم هاتين إلا سدانة الكعبة وسقاية الحج

AZRAQI:v2p121/r3.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p121/r3.speaker: النبي
AZRAQI:v2p121/r3.claim: The Prophet says God has removed pre-Islamic pride and boasting of ancestry: all descend from Adam and the most honored before God are the most pious.
AZRAQI:v2p121/r3.anchor: إلا أن الله سبحانه وتعالى قد أذهب عنكم نخوة الجاهلية وتكبرها بآبائها كلكم لآدم وآدم من تراب وأكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم

AZRAQI:v2p121/r4.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p121/r4.speaker: النبي
AZRAQI:v2p121/r4.claim: For a mistaken quasi-intentional killing with a stick or whip, the Prophet prescribes an aggravated blood payment of one hundred camels, forty carrying young.
AZRAQI:v2p121/r4.anchor: وفي قتيل العصا والسوط الخطأ شبه العمد الدية مغلظة ماية ناقة منها أربعون في بطونها أولادها

AZRAQI:v2p121/r5.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p121/r5.speaker: النبي
AZRAQI:v2p121/r5.claim: The Prophet declares Mecca sacred from the day God created heaven and earth; it was unlawful before and after him, and allowed to him for only one hour that day.
AZRAQI:v2p121/r5.anchor: إلا أن الله قد حرم مكة يوم خلق السموات والأرض فهي حرام بحرام الله سبحانه لم تحل لأحد

AZRAQI:v2p121/r6.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p121/r6.speaker: النبي
AZRAQI:v2p121/r6.claim: The Prophet forbids driving out Mecca's game, cutting its thorn trees or grass, and taking its lost property except by someone who publicly announces it.
AZRAQI:v2p121/r6.anchor: لا ينفر صيدها ولا تعضد عضاها ولا تحل لقطتها إلا لمنشد ولا يختلا خلاها

AZRAQI:v2p121/r7.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p121/r7.speaker: النبي
AZRAQI:v2p121/r7.claim: When al-ʿAbbās asks for an exception for idhkhir, needed by smiths and for house roofs, the Prophet first pauses and then declares it lawful.
AZRAQI:v2p121/r7.anchor: يا رسول الله إلا الأذخر فإنه لا بد منه للقين ولظهور البيت فسكت النبي & ثم قال إلا الأذخر فإنه حلال

AZRAQI:v2p121/r8.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p121/r8.speaker: مناديا
AZRAQI:v2p121/r8.claim: After leaving Mecca, the Prophet sends a herald to proclaim that there is no bequest to an heir.
AZRAQI:v2p121/r8.anchor: فلما هبط النبي & بعث مناديا ينادي ألا لا وصية لوارث

AZRAQI:v2p121/r9.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p121/r9.speaker: مناديا
AZRAQI:v2p121/r9.claim: The herald also proclaims that a child belongs to the marital bed and the adulterer receives the stone.
AZRAQI:v2p121/r9.anchor: بعث مناديا ينادي ألا لا وصية لوارث وأن الولد للفراش وللعاهر الحجر

AZRAQI:v2p121/r10.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p121/r10.speaker: مناديا
AZRAQI:v2p121/r10.claim: The herald further proclaims that a woman may not give away any of her property without her husband's permission.
AZRAQI:v2p121/r10.anchor: فلما هبط النبي & بعث مناديا ينادي ألا لا وصية لوارث وأن الولد للفراش وللعاهر الحجر وأنه لا يحل لامرأة

IBNHISHAM:v2p87#2/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p87#2/r1.speaker: محمود بن لبيد
IBNHISHAM:v2p87#2/r1.claim: At Uhud, two elderly men, Husayl ibn Jabir and Thabit ibn Waqsh, left the fortifications to seek martyrdom; Thabit was killed by polytheists, and Muslims mistakenly killed Husayl without recognizing him.
IBNHISHAM:v2p87#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: وحدثني عاصم بن عمر بن قتادة، عن محمود بن لبيد، قال: لما خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى أحد

IBNHISHAM:v2p87#2/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p87#2/r2.speaker: حذيفة
IBNHISHAM:v2p87#2/r2.claim: When Hudhayfa identified his slain father, he forgave the Muslims; he gave them the blood money the Prophet offered, winning further esteem from the Prophet.
IBNHISHAM:v2p87#2/r2.anchor: فقال حذيفة: أبي ، فقالوا: والله إن عرفناه، وصدقوا. قال حذيفة: يغفر الله لكم وهو أرحم الراحمين
